title: Fragility Assessment of Bovine Cortical Bone Using Scratch Tests
protocol: Collect freshly harvested bovine femurs from a USDA-certified slaughterhouse.
Transport the femurs in plastic air-tight bags in a cooler.
Freeze the femurs at -20°C until specimen preparation.
Thaw the frozen femurs in water for about 2 h at room temperature.
Cut discs about 10-15 mm thick from the mid-diaphysis region using a table top diamond band saw.
Remove any soft tissue or flesh attached to the cortical bone with a dissection kit.
Cut cross sections of the femur along the longitudinal axis using a diamond-wafering blade on a low speed saw under wet conditions.
Clean the specimens in a solution prepared using 1.5% anionic cleaner and 5% bleach for a duration of 20 min in an ultrasonic cleaner.
Coat the walls of the mold with a release agent.
Mix the acrylic resin and hardener in a beaker, as per instructions given by the PMMA manufacturer.
Place one of the cut cortical bone specimens into each mold with the surface to be scratched facing downwards.
Pour the acrylic resin mix into these prepared specimen holders.
Let the specimens cure for a duration of up to 4 - 5 h.
Cut the embedded specimens into 5-mm thick discs, exposing the surface to be scratched, using the low speed saw.
Mount the specimens on aluminum discs of diameter 34 mm and height 5 mm using cyanoacrylate adhesive.
Wrap the specimens in a gauge soaked in Hanks Balanced Saline Solution (HBSS) and refrigerate at 4 °C until further use.
Grind bovine cortical bone specimens using 400 grit Silicon Carbide paper for 1 min at 100 rpm.
Grind the same specimens using 600 grit Silicon Carbide paper for 5 min at 150 rpm.
Machine grind the specimens on 800 grit paper for 15 min at 150 rpm, 60 rpm head speed, and 1 lb operating load.
Machine grind the specimens on 1200 grit paper for 15 min at 150 rpm, 60 rpm head speed, and 1 lb operating load.
Polish the specimens using 3 µm diamond suspension solution on a hard, perforated, non-woven cloth for 90 min at room temperature with 1 lb load, 300 rpm base speed, and 60 rpm head speed.
Polish the specimens using 1 µm diamond suspension solution on a hard, perforated, non-woven cloth for 90 min at room temperature with 1 lb load, 300 rpm base speed, and 60 rpm head speed.
Polish the specimens using 0.25 µm diamond suspension solution on a hard, perforated, non-woven cloth for 90 min at room temperature with 1 lb load, 300 rpm base speed, and 60 rpm head speed.
Polish the specimens using 0.05 µm alumina suspension solution on a soft, synthetic rayon cloth for 90 min at 1 lb load, 100 rpm base speed, and 60 rpm head speed.
Clean residue from specimens with de-ionized water in an ultrasonic bath for 2 min after each grinding and polishing step.
Calibrate the Rockwell indenter tip using polycarbonate as reference material.
Place the cortical bone specimen on the stage.
Choose the site of scratch test using the optical microscope set up integrated to the micro scratch tester module.
Apply a linear progressive load with a start load of 30 mN and end load of 30 N.
Set the loading rate to 60 N/min.
Set the scratch length to 3 mm.
Perform series of scratch tests on short longitudinal bovine cortical bone specimens.
Wet the specimen surface with HBSS after every three to four scratch tests.
